sense: one stage of a game or contest

terms.gloss: a heat, a round (of races or games)
terms.comment: Properly the start, when the chariots were let go; then each race of a day at the circus.

evidence: Traupman 46: congressū vincere, win a round
terms.comment: Classically a meeting, and an encounter in a fight (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a round of turns, a rotation
evidence: Liv. 1.17.6: per omnēs in orbem ībat
terms.comment: in orbem, in turn, round the circle.

phrases.latin: circēnsium diē, quō facilius centum missūs peragerentur, singulōs ē septēnīs spatiīs ad quīna corripuit
phrases.english: on the day of the circus games, so that a hundred races could be got through more easily, he cut each from seven laps to five

phrases.latin: quīnque diērum spatiō fīniēbātur imperium ac per omnēs in orbem ībat
phrases.english: each held power for five days, and it went round them all in turn
